breathing-intro: Let's take two minutes to breathe together. We'll use box breathing. Breathe in slowly for four seconds, hold for four, breathe out for four, and hold again for four. There's nothing else you need to do right now. Let's begin.
breathing-closing: Take one more slow breath. Notice how your body feels. You did it.
affirmation-intro: Take a moment to settle in. I'm going to share a few affirmations with you. After each one, repeat it back to yourself out loud or quietly in your mind. Don't worry about saying it perfectly. Just give yourself a moment to believe the words you're saying. Let's begin.
affirmation-enough: I am enough as I am.
affirmation-handle-present: I can handle what is in front of me.
affirmation-one-step: I am allowed to take things one step at a time.
affirmation-growing: I trust myself to keep growing.
affirmation-not-figured-out: I do not need to have everything figured out today.
affirmation-showing-up: I am proud of myself for showing up.
affirmation-feelings: My feelings are valid, and they do not define my future.
affirmation-begin-again: I can begin again whenever I need to.
affirmation-small-steps: I am becoming stronger through every small step.
affirmation-kindness-to-others: I am worthy of the same kindness I give to others.
affirmation-move-forward: I choose to move forward with patience.
affirmation-closing: Take one last slow breath. You don't have to believe every word perfectly yet. Sometimes practicing kindness toward yourself is enough for today. Carry one of these thoughts with you as you continue your day.
meditation-settle: Find a comfortable position. Let your shoulders relax. You don't need to solve anything for the next few minutes. This moment is simply a chance to slow down. Take a slow breath in, and gently breathe out.
meditation-breathing: Bring your attention to your breathing. You don't need to change it. Simply notice the air coming in, and notice it leaving again. If it feels comfortable, let each breath become a little slower.
meditation-release-tension: Notice where your body may be holding tension. Maybe it's your shoulders, your jaw, your hands, or somewhere else. You don't have to force the tension away. Simply notice it, and allow that part of your body to soften as you exhale.
meditation-thoughts: Thoughts may come into your mind. That's okay. You don't need to follow every thought. Notice it, and gently bring your attention back to your breathing. There is nowhere else you need to be in this moment.
meditation-center: Take another slow breath in. Notice the support beneath you. Notice your body here in this moment. For these next few breaths, give yourself permission to simply be still.
meditation-return: Begin bringing your attention back to the space around you. Notice the sounds around you. Notice your hands and your feet. Take one deeper breath in, and slowly let it go.
meditation-closing: As you finish, remember that you can return to your breath whenever you need a moment to slow down. Move forward gently. You're ready when you are.
